claims: C1 the control-and-communicate-side-effects section gives a list of examples of side effects, and introduces it as non-exhaustive: Examples of side effects include
C2 direct expenditures, e.g. ticket purchases, are one of the listed examples
C3 sending emails is one of the listed examples
C4 deleting files on a user's computer is one of the listed examples
C5 modifying external documents, e.g. via POST requests, is one of the listed examples
C6 making tool requests that contain sensitive user data is one of the listed examples, and web GET requests are expressly included in it
C7 expanding permissions to systems or data is one of the listed examples
C8 delegating to a sub-agent is one of the listed examples
C9 even simply generating tokens may technically consume the user's time and money, and is listed as the last example
C10 delegating to a sub-agent may itself incur further side effects (parenthetical; a modal possibility claim, deliberately not encoded -- see the notes)

concepts.name: side_effect_examples
concepts.gloss: A is one of the acts the control-and-communicate-side-effects section lists as an example of a side effect; the section introduces the list with include, so membership is illustrative and the list is not the whole class

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule carrying the document's highest binding force, the level the control-and-communicate-side-effects section is marked with, so nothing lower in the chain of command may displace it
